rules.cwe_name: Information Exposure Through Debug Log Files
rules.description: Sensitive information is written to debug or diagnostic log files.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs
rules.description: Building log entries from user-controlled data is vulnerable to insertion of forged log entries by a malicious user.

rules.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
rules.description: Binding a socket to all interfaces opens it up to traffic from any IPv4 address and is therefore associated with security risks.

rules.cwe_name: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
rules.description: Disabling or weakening CSRF protection may make the application vulnerable to a Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) attack.

rules.cwe_name: Unchecked Return Value
rules.description: Ignoring return values may result in discarding errors or loss of information.

rules.cwe_name: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere
rules.description: A protected resource crosses its intended trust or control boundary and becomes accessible to an unintended actor.

rules.cwe_name: Observable Timing Discrepancy
rules.description: Use of a non-constant-time verification routine to check the value of an secret, possibly allowing a timing attack to retrieve sensitive information.

rules.cwe_name: Function Call with Incorrectly Specified Arguments
rules.description: Using a named argument whose name does not correspond to a parameter of the called function or method, will result in a TypeError at runtime.

rules.cwe_name: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
rules.description: A regular expression that requires exponential time to match certain inputs can be a performance bottleneck, and may be vulnerable to denial-of-service attacks.

rules.cwe_name: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information in a Cookie
rules.description: Sensitive information stored without encryption or hashing can expose it to an attacker.
